question: Which of the following structures has the IUPAC name 7-hydroxy-5-methylheptan-2-one?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The IUPAC name "7-hydroxy-5-methylheptan-2-one" refers to a structure with a hydroxyl (-OH) group on carbon 7, a methyl (-CH3) group on carbon 5, and a ketone (>C=O) group on carbon 2.
 
• In IUPAC nomenclature, the longest continuous carbon chain is chosen as the parent chain, and substituents are numbered to give the lowest possible locants.
 
• Option 2 correctly represents the structure where the functional groups are located as per the name: hydroxyl at position 7, methyl at position 5, and ketone at position 2.
 
• The numbering begins from the end closest to the ketone group, ensuring it gets the smallest locant (2).
 
• The name adheres to IUPAC conventions, ensuring clarity and standardization in chemical representation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **IUPAC Nomenclature:** It is the standardized system for naming chemical compounds, ensuring consistency across scientific communication globally.
 
• **Functional Groups:** Hydroxyl (-OH), methyl (-CH3), and ketone (>C=O) are common groups that dictate the chemical properties and reactivity of organic compounds.
 
• **Locants:** Numbers assigned to substituents or functional groups indicate their positions on the parent chain in the molecular structure.
 
• **Ketones:** Ketones are organic compounds characterized by the carbonyl group (>C=O) bonded to two carbon atoms. They are commonly used in industry and biological systems.
 
• **Hydroxy Compounds:** Compounds containing hydroxyl groups (-OH) are classified as alcohols or phenols, depending on their structural context, and play a key role in chemical synthesis and biological processes.
